content.text:
<title>Calderwick Museum: interview with the director</title>
<transcript>
[0] Imogen Vasey: My guest is Aurelio Banks, director of the Calderwick Museum, which reopens next month.
[1] Imogen Vasey: Aurelio, the museum has been shut for a long time.
[2] Imogen Vasey: Tell me what happened.
[3] Aurelio Banks: We closed in January last year after a water main burst under the east wing.
[4] Aurelio Banks: The basement flooded to a depth of about a metre.
[5] Aurelio Banks: We moved 9,000 objects out of the stores in four days, most of them by hand, with staff and volunteers working in shifts.
[6] Aurelio Banks: Nothing was lost, which I still find hard to believe.
[7] Aurelio Banks: About 200 objects needed conservation work, mostly paper and textiles that had got damp.
[8] Imogen Vasey: And the building itself?
[9] Aurelio Banks: The building was the bigger problem.
[10] Aurelio Banks: The flood showed us that the wiring in the east wing dated from the 1960s and had to be replaced.
[11] Aurelio Banks: So what began as a repair became a refit of the whole wing.
[12] Aurelio Banks: The work cost 2.4 million pounds.
[13] Aurelio Banks: The insurers paid 1.1 million of that, the council gave 800,000, and we raised the remaining 500,000 from donations.
[14] Aurelio Banks: More than 3,000 people gave money, and the smallest gift was two pounds from a school class.
[15] Imogen Vasey: What will visitors see that is new?
[16] Aurelio Banks: The east wing now has a gallery about the town's mills, which we never had room for before.
[17] Aurelio Banks: It holds a working loom that was built here in 1887 and has not run in public for fifty years.
[18] Aurelio Banks: We have also moved the stores out of the basement to the second floor, so they are above any water.
[19] Aurelio Banks: And for the first time there is a lift, so every floor can be reached without stairs.
[20] Imogen Vasey: When do you open?
[21] Aurelio Banks: We open on the fourteenth of next month.
[22] Aurelio Banks: Entry stays free, as it has been since the museum was founded.
[23] Imogen Vasey: Is there anything you would have done differently?
[24] Aurelio Banks: I would have moved the stores years ago.
[25] Aurelio Banks: We knew the basement was the wrong place for them.
[26] Aurelio Banks: It took a flood to make us do it.
[27] Imogen Vasey: Aurelio Banks, thank you.
[28] Aurelio Banks: Thank you for having me.
</transcript>

points.text: The Calderwick Museum closed in January last year after a water main burst under the east wing, flooding the basement to about a metre deep.
About 9,000 objects were moved out of the stores in four days, mostly by hand, by staff and volunteers working in shifts.
Nothing was lost, though about 200 objects needed conservation work, mostly damp paper and textiles.
The flood revealed that the east wing's wiring dated from the 1960s and had to be replaced, so the repair became a refit of the whole wing.
The work cost 2.4 million pounds: 1.1 million from insurers, 800,000 from the council and 500,000 from donations.
More than 3,000 people donated, and the smallest gift was two pounds from a school class.
The east wing now has a new gallery about the town's mills, including a working loom built at the museum in 1887 that has not run in public for fifty years.
The stores have been moved from the basement to the second floor, above any water, and a lift now gives step-free access to every floor for the first time.
The museum reopens on the fourteenth of next month, and entry remains free as it has been since the museum was founded.
Banks says he would have moved the stores years earlier, as they knew the basement was the wrong place, but it took a flood to make them do it.
